purpose: Realistic NestJS module shapes, with what a correct extractor must read from each. The measurable is not accuracy but SILENCE: which shapes are read as empty, because that is how this feature fails without anyone noticing.

shapes.why: The textbook shape every tutorial shows.
Every configurable module in the ecosystem. The decorator is empty and the wiring is in the return value.
The async registration shape, whose providers are custom objects with an inject array.
The forFeature shape, where an import is a call expression rather than a bare class.
A second decorator above @Module must not hide it.
Circular module references are written as a call, and must not be dropped.
A module can export another module, not only a provider.
A large module often lifts its provider list into a const. A syntax-only extractor cannot follow the reference, and must be honest about that rather than silently reporting nothing.
shapes.knownLimitation: Shorthand property with an identifier initializer: the array is not in the decorator. Reported as a module with no bindings.

shapes.why: Conditional or composed provider lists use a spread.
shapes.knownLimitation: The spread element is recorded verbatim; its contents are not resolved.

shapes.why: The reason the feature exists: a string token invisible to any import graph.
A controller is an injection site too.
@Optional() sits alongside @Inject and must not displace the token.
An ordinary class with a constructor is not an injection site, and recording it pollutes the graph.
